findings.description: The R2 seam mutation recognises only a BACKTICKED anchor, while C-5's own rubric tells the checker punctuation does not count — so an implementation that quotes the anchor with !r, the house style everywhere else in this linter, passes C-5 and fails C-9 with a message saying the opposite of what is true. STRIP_ANCHOR_WRAPPER is `re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", "", ...)`; C-9's text says only "wrapped so the quoted anchor is stripped" and C-5's rubric says "Judge the sentences, not their punctuation". check-job-spec.py already quotes matched text with !r in R3 (`that line is a heading ({target_line.strip()!r})`, :983) and R12' (`for the same restated fact ({excerpt!r})`, :1916), so !r is the reading a worker following the file's own conventions reaches for. Worse, wrapper_is_live — added this round precisely to catch a wrapper that lands without taking effect — reports `ok` on that implementation: its assertion is `return bool(line) and "`" not in line` (probe.py:802), which cannot tell "the wrapper stripped the anchor" from "there was never a backtick to strip". The liveness check is blind in exactly the direction that matters, which is suspicion 1 realised one level up. FIX: strip by VALUE, not by delimiter — wrap r2_anchor_message so it removes its own `anchor` argument from the string it returns — and make wrapper_is_live assert the anchor TEXT is present in the unwrapped diagnostic and absent from the wrapped one. Failing that, C-5 and C-9 must both say the anchor is quoted in backticks, and C-5's "judge the sentences, not their punctuation" has to go.
findings.evidence: Venue /tmp/conaudit-r5-reprpair-XalBV3 (faithful implementation, anchor quoted with !r, plus an N3 suite case asserting `repr(ANCHOR_SNIPPET) in err`). Suite: '324 passed, 0 failed'. probe.py suite-coverage: 'ok R2 diagnostic: `r2_anchor_message` exists as the seam' / 'ok R2 diagnostic: wrapper spliced above the entry guard' / 'ok R2 diagnostic: the wrapper actually strips at runtime' / 'FAIL R2 diagnostic: removing the quoted anchor turns the suite red  rc=0 — no case asserts the anchor is quoted'. C-5 on the same tree: GREEN (rc=0), [A] and [B] both reading "the anchor matched was 'if len(val) >= 2 and val[0] == val[-1]:', quoted at tasks/T-001.md:24". Control that wrapper_is_live is not inert in general: venue /tmp/conaudit-r5-decoy-oQSIaQ (named seam nothing calls) → 'FAIL R2 diagnostic: the wrapper actually strips at runtime  the anchor is still quoted after wrapping'.

findings.description: The named command reads nothing in the state the deliverable is actually in, and the clause says nothing about an empty result. `git diff $(git merge-base main HEAD)..HEAD -- .agent-guild/scripts/test_check_job_spec.py` reads COMMITTED history; nothing in the guild lifecycle commits a worker's output — the worker writes files and sets `needs-check`, and the checker is dispatched against that working tree. r4's finding was the mirror of this and its recommended fix carried two halves; the round adopted the base ref and dropped "an empty diff is a FAIL of this clause rather than a pass", so a checker handed a conforming, uncommitted implementation reads zero lines and is told to "rule on each case added for the three changes". It either fails correct work or improvises. The same commit that makes C-10 readable empties C-7, so the two clauses now require mutually exclusive git states (see the C-7 finding). FIX: have the rubric name both reads and say what an empty one means — run the merge-base diff, and when it is empty run `git diff -- .agent-guild/scripts/test_check_job_spec.py` plus `git status --porcelain` for the untracked case; if BOTH are empty the job added no cases and that is a FAIL of this clause, not a pass.
findings.evidence: Venue /tmp/conaudit-r5-ref-SWwdku, on branch feat/193-linter-three-shapes with a full reference implementation in the working tree. Uncommitted: `git diff $(git merge-base main HEAD)..HEAD -- .agent-guild/scripts/test_check_job_spec.py | wc -l` → 0, while check-diff-scope reports 'OK: 6 path(s) in scope'. After `git commit`: the same diff → 128 lines and readable (N1/N2/N3 cases visible), while check-diff-scope reports 'OK: 0 path(s) in scope'. merge-base resolves (ae3f757efd50a3d0af05265b5837b6df94e2bc63) and the command also works from a detached HEAD (128 lines), so `main` resolution is not the problem — the commit boundary is.

findings.description: The second seam C-9 imposes is never declared, and the implementation it refuses is one C-1 and C-2 both certify. C-9 spells out the R2 constraint — "That is a seam this clause imposes deliberately" — and says of R10 only "`_governs_plural_noun`, reverted to its strict pre-job body". Nothing tells a worker the relaxation has to LIVE in that predicate. The spec's own "Start here" names two sites, `:1291-1293` for `_governs_plural_noun` and `:1303` for `find_r10_violation`, so putting the modifier walk in the caller is a reading the paperwork invites. I built it: the predicate keeps its exact shipped body and a caller-side helper decides adjacency. C-1 green through every adjective and every nonce, C-2 green across all eleven archives, and an archive-drawn N1 case that goes red the moment the relaxation is removed — and C-9 red, at blocker severity, with a bare `FAIL R10 relaxation: revert to strict adjacency landed` and an EMPTY detail string, because revert_adjacency correctly reports its no-op. The worker is told nothing about what to change. This is r3's finding recurring: that round repaired the guard that reported a no-op revert as landed, and left the clause silent about why the predicate has to be the seam. FIX: say it in C-9's text the way the R2 seam is said — the adjacency decision must be made inside `_governs_plural_noun`, because reverting that body is what separates a case for the relaxation from a case for R10 generally — and give probe.py:749's ok() a detail naming it.
findings.evidence: Venue /tmp/conaudit-r5-r10caller2-WUYdaE (relaxation in find_r10_violation via `_count_governs_a_plural_noun`, predicate byte-identical to its shipped body, reference R21 and R2 plus all three archive-drawn suite cases). C-1 GREEN (rc=0), C-2 GREEN (rc=0), C-9 RED (rc=1): 'ok R10 relaxation: `_governs_plural_noun` is still the predicate' then 'FAIL R10 relaxation: revert to strict adjacency landed  ' — detail empty. Reference implementation with the same relaxation inside the predicate (/tmp/conaudit-r5-ref-SWwdku): C-9 all fifteen assertions ok.

findings.description: C-7 is now the other half of C-10's contradiction, and its vacuity has stopped being hypothetical. check-diff-scope.py builds its path set from `git status --porcelain` union `git diff --name-only`, both working-tree only, so against a committed implementation it reports 'OK: 0 path(s) in scope' and exits 0 — the clause's own failing example, a stray edit to dispatch-guard.py, rides straight through. r4 filed this as a minor scope note because nothing in the constitution pushed a worker toward committing. C-10's repair now does, in so many words ("so the diff survives the work being committed"), which makes the vacuous state the one a worker following the constitution will be in. FIX: pin the order in C-7's text — this check runs against the uncommitted working tree, before anything is committed — or give C-7 the same merge-base base C-10 now names, so both clauses read the same tree.
findings.evidence: Venue /tmp/conaudit-r5-ref-SWwdku. Uncommitted: 'check-diff-scope: in scope: .agent-guild/scripts/check-job-spec.py ... OK: 6 path(s) in scope' (rc=0). Same tree after `git commit`: 'OK: 0 path(s) in scope' (rc=0). Both are a PASS of C-7; only the first is a check.

findings.description: The repair to r4's stale-claim finding made the claim strictly more falsifiable and strictly false. "Every SCRIPT-checked clause below runs a probe at `.agent-guild/state/checks/probe.py` rather than reading the test suite" is wrong for three of the eight script-checked clauses: C-6 runs `test_check_job_spec.py`, `--self-test`, `test_hooks.py` and `build-plugin.py --check`; C-7 runs `check-diff-scope.py`; C-8 runs an importtime/AST one-liner. None of the three touches probe.py, and C-6 does run the test suite, which the second half of the sentence denies. The previous wording ("Every behavioral clause") was vague enough to be arguable; narrowing it to "SCRIPT-checked" named a set anyone can enumerate and got the set wrong. The decompose step reads this preamble into worker briefs. FIX: "Every clause that checks a BEHAVIOR of the linter — C-1 through C-4 and C-9 — runs a probe at ...; C-6, C-7 and C-8 check the tree around it and invoke existing commands; C-5 and C-10 are rubrics."

findings.description: One run in nine, one of C-1's three nonces is a token any implementation satisfies, including the strict predicate the clause exists to reject. probe.py:236-239 draws each nonce as 4-9 random lowercase letters with no constraint on the last one; a nonce ending in `s` IS the plural noun as far as `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*s\b` is concerned, so `Four qwerts rules constrain how:` fires R10 on the untouched tree and the assertion `fires through 'qwerts'` passes against an implementation that changed nothing. P(at least one of three ends in `s`) = 1 - (25/26)^3 = 10.8%, measured at 10.785% over 20,000 draws. C-1 still discriminates as a whole — the five fixed adjectives carry it — but the nonce exists specifically to close the allowlist hole, and one in nine runs it closes nothing while reporting `ok`. The same unseeded draw makes a failure unreproducible: a worker who fails on `fires through 'zatfmkl'` gets a different token on the next run and cannot diff the two. FIX: reject a draw ending in `s` and redraw, and print the drawn nonces once at the top of the probe's output so a FAIL can be replayed.
findings.evidence: Measured against the untouched tree: 'UNTOUCHED (strict) linter, nonce="qwerts": R10 fired=True rc=4' versus 'nonce="qwertx": R10 fired=False rc=0'. Collision rate over 20,000 draws of the probe's own generator: 2157/20000 = 10.785%. Untouched-tree baseline run drew 'ldbw', 'upfl', 'zatfmkl' (probe.py:236-239, apparatus/CON-audit-r5/baseline/r10-adjective.err).

findings.description: The r5 revision note misplaces the decoy `__main__` literal, and the misplacement hides a real fragility. "the literal occurs twice; the first is inside the self-test's fixture strings" — it is not. The first occurrence is check-job-spec.py:161, inside a module-level COMMENT ("validate-verdict.py has no `if __name__ == \"__main__\":`-gated side effects"), several hundred lines ABOVE every definition the wrapper needs. That matters because splice_wrapper's rfind falls back to it: with the real guard absent, splice_wrapper returns True and splices the wrapper into the comment block at :161, where `r2_anchor_message` is not yet defined, so the linter raises NameError on every invocation and C-9 reports 'the anchor is still quoted after wrapping'. FIX: correct the note to name :161 as a comment, and have splice_wrapper refuse an anchor that sits above the definition it wraps.
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'if __name__' .agent-guild/scripts/check-job-spec.py` → 161 (comment) and 2400 (the guard); the file is 2401 lines. Venue /tmp/conaudit-r5-splice-aLOhWg: with the guard deleted, splice_wrapper → True; with the guard spelled with single quotes, splice_wrapper → False (C-9 then reports 'no `if __name__` guard to splice above').

findings.description: "firing R3 four rules ahead of R2" is off by one against the shipped rule order. run_rules' `steps` tuple runs R3 at index 12 and R2 at index 15, with R8 and R16 between them — three rules ahead, not four. It becomes four only once R21 lands in the slot this job adds, and the sentence is explaining why TODAY's fixtures had to be synthetic. findings.description: Both r4 majors are fixed and the rubric now decides the cases it claimed to. The exit-code gate is real: an implementation with the silence guard removed exits 1 and prints its own violating diagnostic under [C], so the case r4 showed sliding through is now settled before the checker reads prose. The count matches what it counts — three blocks printed, three blocks named — and [C] reads exactly `(nothing emitted)` when R2 is silent, which it can only do when no R2 line exists in stderr. The three judgment variants I built are all refusable on the printed output: an implementation that omits the position when it equals the citation's, r3's `is not on that line` phrasing, and one that gives no position at all — each prints a [B] block a checker can hold against the block header's stated document line. findings.description: Scope of this round. Every one of the eight script-checked clauses ran twice — against the tree as I found it, and against a reference implementation of all three changes plus three archive-drawn suite cases built from the constitution and the documents it names — and each got at least one variant built to violate its own text; seventeen variants in all. C-5 and C-10 are rubrics with nothing to execute, so both were judged by reading, with C-5's instrument run against four implementations to see what its checker would actually be handed and C-10's named command run against a real committed and uncommitted tree. check-baselines.py reported 'ran 8 (3 red, 5 green), skipped 2 (2 judgment, 0 no-baseline)' and exited 0; I re-derived all eight by hand and the declared baselines are accurate. The weight line's reason holds: probe.py is 854 lines, this round did rebuild a full reference implementation, and C-10 names a property no existing command checks — deep has no ceiling, so no overrun line is owed, and there is no **Lint exception** line to audit. The constitution's own state passes check-job-spec.py --audit-id CON-audit. Working tree verified clean by `git status --porcelain` at the start and at filing; everything built or acted on lived outside the repo.
